messages.content: write a story about a note that two friends understand in a different way. keep it simple, but let them work out the meaning together.

two friends walk into a garden near the library. there is a note on a small table. it says: please leave the flowers here. one friend thinks someone has brought flowers and wants them to stay on the table. the other thinks the note is asking people not to take flowers from the garden. they look around. there are no flowers on the table, but there are flowers growing near it. they go to the library and ask a worker about the note. she says that people sometimes take flowers from the garden. the note asks them to leave the growing flowers where they are. the friends return to the garden and sit near the table without taking any flowers.
was the first friend wrong to ask what the note was about?
no. the note could have more than one meaning without more context. asking the worker helped the friends find out what was wanted.
why was the empty table important?
it gave them a reason to question the idea that someone had brought flowers to put there. however, an empty table alone did not tell them the whole meaning of the note.
make the note easy to understand for people who have just come to the garden.
please do not take the flowers from this garden. leave them here for everyone to enjoy.
what did the friends do after they understood?
they went back to the garden and sat near the table. they did not take any flowers.
what does hold my place in this book mean?
it can mean helping you keep the page where you stopped reading, so you can find it again. for example, someone could keep a hand on that page while you get a card to put there.
write a story with that request and a brother who asks what to do.

a girl is reading a long story. she wants to get a card from her desk, but she does not want to lose her page. she asks her brother to hold her place in the book. he asks whether he should carry the book to another room. she says no and puts her hand by the line where she stopped. he keeps the book open while she gets the card. she puts the card between the pages and thanks him. now she can close the book and find her place later.
why did he ask a question?
he did not know what she wanted him to do. asking helped him understand before he moved the book.
did she want him to hold a place in a line of people?
no. the context is reading a book. her place is the part she wants to return to, rather than a place where a person stands.
write her request with more detail.
please keep this book open at this page while i get a card from my desk.
i want to read a whole book today, but i only have a little free time. help me make a plan that does not say i must finish it.

you could choose a few pages to read during your free time. after those pages, check how much time you still have. if there is more time, keep reading. if not, keep your place and return to the book later.
i still want to finish the book one day. does this plan lose that goal?
no. the whole book can still be your goal while a few pages are the task for now. doing a smaller part helps you do some of the work needed for the larger goal.
write a note i can leave inside the book.
read a few pages today. keep the place where you stop. return when you have more time.
should the note say that a few pages are enough to know the whole story?
no. reading a few pages gives you part of the story. it does not mean you know the whole book. the note is about doing some reading with the time you have.
say that last idea simply.
the note helps you do some reading now and return for more later.
what is the difference between she held a cup and she carried a cup to the kitchen?
she held a cup says that the cup was in her hand or hands. she carried a cup to the kitchen also says that she moved it to the kitchen. held alone does not tell us where she went.
can someone carry a cup without walking?
yes. a person could carry a cup while riding in a vehicle, for example. carrying something does not always mean walking.
write a short story with held and carries in different parts of the day.
in the morning, a woman held an empty cup while she waited for tea. now it is afternoon, and she carries a cup of water to the garden. she puts it on a table and sits down to read.
was it the same cup?
the story does not tell us. it says a cup in each part, so we should not be sure that the two cups are the same one.
change it so we know it is the same cup.
in the morning, a woman held an empty cup while she waited for tea. now it is afternoon, and she carries that same cup, with water in it, to the garden. she puts it on a table and sits down to read.
a picture of my school is on the wall. the library is on the left in the picture. does that mean it is on my left when i stand outside the school?
not always. which way are you looking? which side of the school can you see in the picture? left in a picture does not always mean left from every place outside.
can you explain without using a map?

think of two people standing face to face. one person can hold up their left hand. the other person sees that hand on their right. where you stand and which way you look are important when using left and right.
i want to tell a friend where the library door is. what detail would help?
say where your friend should stand and which way to look before saying left or right. you can also name something near the door, such as a tree or a table, if it is really there.
write a message if the library door is next to a large tree.
the library door is next to the large tree. when you reach the tree, look for the door next to it.
can you make the message shorter?
look for the large tree. the library door is next to it.
my family has a photo with my mother, father, and sister in it. i took the photo. does the picture show everyone who was there?
no. you were there to take it, but you are not in the picture as you said. a photo can leave out someone who was there.
my brother was at home. can you say he was there too because he is in my family?
no. being in your family does not mean he was at the place where you took the photo. you said that he was at home.
write a clear message that keeps these facts apart.
my mother, father, and sister are in the photo. i was there too, but i took the picture. my brother was at home.
how many people did i say were at the place where i took it?
you said that four people were there: your mother, your father, your sister, and you. that does not tell us whether other people were there as well.
why not say only four?
you gave information about four people, but you did not say that nobody else was there.
can a person have a warm drink in a cold room, or is that wrong grammar?
yes, a person can have a warm drink in a cold room. the sentence is clear. warm is about the drink, and cold is about the room. the two words are about different things.
give the answer in fewer words.
yes. the drink can be warm while the room is cold. warm and cold are about different things in that sentence.
write a small story with that idea.

a woman comes into a cold room with a warm cup of tea. she puts a blanket over her legs and sits near the window. her friend asks if the tea is cold too. she says no. the room is cold, but she just made the tea. they read together while she drinks it.
does her blanket make the room warm?
the story does not say that. the blanket is over her legs. she can use it while the room is still cold.
say that last part simply.
she can use the blanket while the room is still cold.
i wrote a long letter and got a short reply. does that mean the person did not care?
a short reply alone does not tell you that. the person may have little time or may use fewer words. you would need more context to understand their reason.
they said thank you for telling me. i need time to think. what do those words say?
they thank you for what you told them and say that they need time to think. they have not given a longer answer yet.
help me reply without asking them to answer right away.
thank you for reading it. take the time you need. we can talk more when you are ready.
can you make it sound more like a short message to a friend?
thanks for reading it. take your time. we can talk when you are ready.
what did i ask you to change?
you asked for a reply that sounds more like a short message to a friend. i changed thank you to thanks and made another part shorter.
can we know that the person will answer tomorrow?
no. they said that they need time, but they did not give a day.
i have one piece of bread. i cut it into three pieces. did i get more bread?
you have more pieces, but you have not added bread. the same bread is now in three smaller parts.
if i eat one piece, how many pieces are left?
two pieces are left, if you started with those three and ate one of them.
my friend has another piece and gives it to me. what can i say now?
you can say that you have three pieces left: the two from your bread and the one your friend gave you. this time, you did receive more bread.
are the three pieces all the same size?
we do not know. your original three pieces were not said to be the same size, and your friend could give you a larger or smaller piece.
write a short explanation of why knowing the number of pieces is not enough to know how much bread there is.
one large piece can have more bread than two small pieces. to know how much bread there is, we need more information than the number of pieces.
make that answer shorter.
one large piece can have more bread than two small pieces. knowing the number of pieces alone does not tell us how much bread there is.
ask me a question about my day that i can answer in my own words.
what did you enjoy most today?
lunch.
what did you enjoy about lunch?
i sat with my cousin. please do not make this a story yet.
okay. you enjoyed sitting with your cousin at lunch. would you like to tell me more, or talk about something else?
talk about something else. ask me about tomorrow.
is there something you want to do tomorrow?
i want to read in the garden if the weather is good.
that sounds like a quiet plan. do you already have a book you want to read?
yes, but do not ask another question. just reply to what i said.
you have a book ready and would like to read it in the garden tomorrow if the weather is good.
write a story using grows for a tree and grows for a child, without saying they are the same kind of thing.

a child visits a garden with her grandfather every year. near the door, a tree grows from a small plant into a larger tree. the child grows too. each year, she can reach a little more of the wall next to it. one day, she asks whether the tree grows in the same way she does. her grandfather says that they are different living things. both change as they grow, but a tree does not become a person, and a person does not become a tree.
can you make the story shorter and keep the idea about growing?

a child visits a tree with her grandfather each year. the tree grows, and the child grows too. she asks whether they are the same. he says no. a tree and a person are different living things, even though both grow.
why does the same word work for both?
grows can be used when different living things become larger. using the same word does not say that those things are the same in every way.
what detail in the first story helps us see that the child is larger than before?
she can reach more of the wall each year. that detail helps us understand that she has become larger.
help me write a message. i will meet my friend at the library tomorrow morning, and i want them to bring the book i left at their house.
i will meet you at the library tomorrow morning. could you bring the book i left at your house?
change it so i ask for my card instead. keep the time and place the same.
i will meet you at the library tomorrow morning. could you bring the card i left at your house?
now ask them to bring both things.
i will meet you at the library tomorrow morning. could you bring the book and the card i left at your house?
make it clear that the book is mine, but the card is theirs.
i will meet you at the library tomorrow morning. could you bring my book and your card?
what information did the last change leave out?
the last message does not say where you left the book. it keeps the meeting time, the place, and the request to bring the two things.
could you make the last message sound more like a question about helping me?
when we meet at the library tomorrow morning, could you bring my book and your card, please?
